newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA SAYS '96 SALES UP 24.6 PCT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA SAYS '96 SALES UP 24.6 PCT.

text.p: Czech Skoda Auto a.s., majority-owned by Volkswagen AG, on Monday said that its car sales for 1996 hit 261,067, an increase of 24.6 percent over the previous year.
Skoda added in a statement that it is forecasting sales and production to rise "about 30 percent" in 1997.
"We expect that for 1997, produtction and sales will rise by about 30 percent to at least 340,000 vehicles," a company statement said.
"This dynamic growth will be secured by the full start of production of the Octavia model, which should hit 60,000 units and further growth in the production of the Felicia model," it added.
The statement said that unit sales in the Czech Republic alone for the year totalled 87,398, a year-on-year increase of about 21.3 percent.
Earlier on Monday, a Skoda spokesman told Reuters that the firm's production hit a record 263,193 units, an increase of some 26.3 percent, year-on-year.
Skoda, which posted a 1.6 billion crown loss in 1995, said it does not expect to post a loss again in 1996.
